$comment: The namespaces a bring-your-own chart may never target. ONE list, read by the runner (go:embed in byo.go) and mirrored by the console (apps/console/lib/validations/byo-reserved-namespaces.ts, deep-equal parity test in tests/lib/validations/byo-reserved-namespaces.test.ts). Each group is checked against its source as follows. kubernetes: fixed by hand, each name asserted refused. platformTemplates: EQUALITY (go test, byo_test.go) with the namespaces rendered from infra/templates/argocd/*.yaml. platformCategories: EQUALITY (go test, byo_test.go) with the literal namespace of every helm_release / helm_template block in infra/templates/**/*.tf. platformRuntime: EQUALITY (go test, byo_test.go) with a HAND-KEPT list of the runner's namespace constants in that test - a new constant is not seen until it is added there. platformWorkloads: EQUALITY (go test, byo_oci_test.go) with ByoLegacyDefaultNamespace, and the provisioner's appNamespace - where the first-class workloads, their binding Secrets and service accounts live - is asserted refused for this group's reason (go test, provisioner/byo_move_test.go); a BYO chart with no namespace of its own deploys into byo-<chart id> instead. marketplaceAddOns: EQUALITY with ADDON_CATALOG (console vitest) and EQUALITY with the union of test/e2e/fixtures/addon_catalog.*.json (go test). platformByoDBUsers: EQUALITY (go test, provisioner/byo_db_users_test.go) with manifests.ByoDBUsersNamespace; the exact name only, not an alethia- prefix, so no namespace an existing chart is attached in becomes reserved. prefixes: hand-kept; vcluster- is pinned to the provisioner constant (go test). Kept sorted.

groups.reason: it is a Kubernetes system namespace
the platform's own controllers (ArgoCD, cert-manager, External Secrets, ingress, DNS, autoscaling) install there
the platform's own infrastructure modules (Datadog, Grafana, cluster networking and storage) install there
the platform runs its own components there
the platform's BYO database users Job runs there, with the credentials it needs
the platform's own workloads, their Secrets and their service accounts run there
a platform-managed add-on from the marketplace installs there

prefixes.reason: Kubernetes reserves the kube- prefix for its system namespaces
the platform names every virtual cluster's host namespace vcluster-<name>
